lines.text: Naaman, Aram's army commander, was a leper, and a captive Israelite girl told his wife about the prophet in Samaria.
Naaman carried a letter from the king of Aram to the king of Judah, who tore his clothes.
Elisha's messenger told Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan, and Naaman did so and was clean.
Elisha refused Naaman's gift, so Naaman asked for as much soil as two mules could carry.
Gehazi took silver and clothing from Naaman, told Elisha he had gone to Bethel, and left leprous.
